title: Tavern / shop quirk
_note: Phase 9.6 Tavern oracle: one memorable quirk that makes the stop stick — the last line of a composed sign × specialty × quirk. Full sentences with terminal punctuation. Situational only — never names or stats an NPC. All weight 1.

entries.value: The floor slopes so drinks slide toward the hearth.
A one-eyed cat rules the best seat by the fire.
There's a back room that's always somehow booked.
The keeper never once smiles.
A wall of old weapons hangs above the bar.
Someone is always asleep in the corner.
The drink is good; the roof leaks worse.
A parrot repeats things it shouldn't have heard.
The prices change with the keeper's mood.
Every mug is a different size, and it matters.
A locked cellar door is never explained.
The regulars fall silent when strangers enter.
Payment is expected up front, no exceptions.
A minstrel plays the same three songs, badly.
The stairs creak a warning of anyone coming up.
A tab-book thick as a bible sits behind the bar.
A hound sleeps across the doorway and won't move.
The windows stay shuttered even at noon.
A hatch behind the bar leads who-knows-where.
The keeper remembers every face — and every debt.
The best table is reserved for someone never named.
The clientele keep their hoods up indoors.
A brawl breaks out here most nights, on schedule.
The cellar floods when it rains, and it's raining.
A stuffed bear by the door wears a real crown.
House rule: no weapons, no exceptions, no trust.
A chalkboard lists the dead who still owe.
The mead is watered, but the welcome isn't.
Everyone here seems to be waiting for someone.
The signboard outside says a different name.
The fire never goes out, and no one is seen to feed it.
A row of keys hangs by the door, and none are labelled.
The ale is served in horns; there are no cups to be had.
Every clock in the room shows a different hour.
The guest book has names that were never crossed out.
The last stool at the bar is always left empty.
Someone has carved a warning into every tabletop.
The rooms upstairs are numbered, but not in order.
The bread is fresh; the news is a week stale.
Coins are bitten before they're taken.
The rafters are hung with boots no one has come back for.
No one here sits with their back to the door.
A single candle burns before an empty chair, always.
The mirror behind the bar shows the room a breath too late.
